description.narrative: (Uzbekistan): With FY2022 funding, ADA will focus its value chain development activities on advancing four value chains: aquaculture, cattle, horticulture, and agritourism. The activity will improve, diversify, and scale-up successful interventions conducted in FY 2021 to promote rural women and youth empowerment, with a focus on women at-risk and survivors of gender-based violence (GBV). The activity will assist training graduates to secure internships and employment with local businesses, as well as offer select entrepreneurial graduates with opportunities to access equipment to launch their business enterprises. The activity will also complete six undergraduate and graduate courses for integration in the curricula of Uzbekistan agricultural institutions of higher education and will scale-up professor field day events, domestic study tours, and joint research projects to advance linkages between academia and the private sector. Finally, the activity will collaborate with the Ministry of Agriculture, donor community, and other key stakeholders to introduce and/or improve policies and legislation to promote agricultural land reform, and the growth and development of agritourism, agricultural cooperatives, public-private partnerships (PPPs), and/or public sector agriculture extension services. The activity supports Uzbekistan's ICS Mission Objective 2.2 Advance economic reforms that deliver a sustainable, inclusive, and equitable market-based economy and contributes to the Small and Medium Sized Enterprises, Young and Emerging Leaders, Gender Equality/Women's Empowerment Secondary, Trade Capacity Building, Private Sector Engagement, and Engagement of Higher Education Institutions key issues. The activity also supports USAID/Uzbekistan's Strategic Framework Development Objective 3: Sustainable and Inclusive Economic Growth Enhanced.
